newsitem.title: TURKEY: SOCCER-FANS FORCE TURKISH TV WATCHDOG TO BACKTRACK ON SHUTDOWNS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FANS FORCE TURKISH TV WATCHDOG TO BACKTRACK ON SHUTDOWNS.

text.p: Turkey's television watchdog decided on Wednesday to postpone one-day shutdowns on two channels to allow them to cover vital European soccer matches involving Galatasaray and Fenerbahce.

The country's High Board of Radio and Television (RTUK) had announced a one-day ban on private station InterStar for broadcasting a violent film at prime time and on Show TV because of a legal technicality.

But the shutdown would have deprived Turkish viewers of Thursday's Cup Winners' Cup tie between Galatasaray and Paris St Germain in Istanbul, and the Champions' League clash between Manchester United and Fenerbahce in Manchester on October 30.
On Wednesday the RTUK backed down in the face of pressure from Turkey's fanatical supporters.

"We were a bit careless with the scheduling and following strong reaction from the viewers over the past two days we have just now decided to put back the closures for one day each," the head of RTUK, Gunes Muftuoglu, said.
Turks are obsessive about soccer. A huge proportion of the country's 60 million people support one of the four top teams -- Fenerbahce, Galatasaray, Trabzonspor and Besiktas.
Last week Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan postponed his address to the nation so that a friendly between Turkey and France could be broadcast live from Paris.

Thousands of Turks rushed to buy the relatively expensive pay channel Cine 5 after it was awarded live broadcast rights for Turkish league and UEFA matches. Show TV, a sister channel of Cine 5, sometimes screens UEFA ties.
